body:
Hi Konste, thanks for letting me know!

It seems that the default `bazel-*` symlinks are not symlinked in the execroot but when specifying `--symlink_prefix=.build/` the second invocation (after taking a long time) symlinks the .build folder in the execroot causing the infinite symlink loop.

I'm wondering how other OS scenarios are not hurt by this.

Two more observations.
1. When I shutdown bazel after the .build symlink is created inside execroot, and reboot bazel again it seems to work properly.
2. I never get the exception you listed. Maybe that's due to my permissive path length settings?

I have a feeling that the watcher incorrectly registers the .build folder to be watched when it's created.

Tom, thank you for looking into this! 
What setting do you mean when you said `my permissive path length settings`?

I'm referring to the LongPathsEnabled setting that allows paths longer than 260 characters. It's just a guess to why I'm not seeing the same error. I do encounter a very long loading times so there's definitely something going wrong.
So I have checked and apparently I have LongPathsEnabled setting enabled on my Windows machines. And still I see the warning `Error encountered with local file system watcher...` periodically.

The only warning I encounter every now and then (e.g. after big checkouts) is "WARNING: Overflow when watching local filesystem for changes... temporarily falling back to manually checking files for changes". Are you still seeing "The name of the file cannot be resolved by the system"?

We also mostly see `WARNING: Overflow when watching local filesystem for changes...` now.
@tomdegoede Any chance you can do something to make it more reliable?

issue.title: Take windows junctions into account with --watchfs

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Related PR: #11334 I enabled --watchfs for windows under --experimental_windows_watchfs. 

Related issues: #11619:
1. (infinite) recursion occurs on the convenience symlinks when they are created while watch is active. This also causes a delay on the first bazel invocation after the symlinks are created.
2. quite often an overflow warning occurs `WARNING: Overflow when watching local filesystem for changes...`. I think this is because the watcher also watches the bazel-* symlinks with many file changes due to being output directories.

The reason that this behavior is different on windows seems to be that the convenience symlinks are actually created as junctions. I have tried changed this logic to creating actually directory symlinks which seemed to resolve the issues. This however could be a breaking change on some systems because creating symlinks requires more privileges than creating junctions.

~~Therefore I propose the following changes:~~
~~1. Watch the root directory non-recursively. As it's done on non windows systems.~~
~~2. Watch each direct sub-directory recursively. Excluding junctions.~~

~~The downside of this approach is that the convenience symlinks must be at the root of the workspace. When using --symlink_prefix with a sub-directory (which is the case for in the linked issue) both issues would still occur.~~

I have updated the PR to reflect my comment below because this also resolves the above mentioned downside and is a simpler solution. I have tested several scenarios with regards to the folder locking but was able to delete workspace folders from explorer, ide and cli every time.

body: @konste @tomdegoede Was this fixed by https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/0cdd71fe9782c7817fc1e0294285699fb4db8040 or is this still an issue?
The fix should be in 3.7.0. right? I am going to test it today and get back to you. The issue was intermittent, so it would take a full day to make sure.

This is confusing: description of [0cdd71f](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/0cdd71fe9782c7817fc1e0294285699fb4db8040) contains this paragraph in strikethrough font: ~~The downside of this approach is that the convenience symlinks must be at the root of the workspace. When using --symlink_prefix with a sub-directory (which is the case for in the linked issue) both issues would still occur.~~

Current issue #11619 is specifically about using both flags together `--experimental_windows_watchfs` and `--symlink_prefix`. If the paragraph above is true, then current issue is NOT fixed. But strikethrough font confuses me. 

@tomdegoede could you please clarify? 

My best guess at the moment is that the current issue is not fixed.
@konste please refer to #12054. It implements a second solution (hence the strikethrough) that should also have resolved your issue.
